title: Branch
summary: A branch is a movable name for a line of commits, so you can work on something new without touching main.

levels.title: Make a branch
levels.briefing: A branch is just a label pointing at a commit. git branch <name> creates a new label at the commit you are on. It does not switch to it: HEAD, the marker for where you are, stays on your current branch.
levels.objective: Create a branch called feature, and stay on main.

cheatsheet.description: List branches; * marks the current one
Create a branch at another commit

hints: git branch with a name creates a branch.
It will point at the same commit as main.
levels.successMessage: The graph shows feature and main on the same commit. HEAD is still on main.

levels.title: Two branches
levels.objective: Create two branches: bugfix and experiment.
hints: Each branch needs its own git branch command.
Both will point at the current commit.
Run: git branch bugfix, then git branch experiment
levels.successMessage: Branches cost almost nothing, so it is normal to have several.

levels.title: Clean up
levels.objective: The branch old-idea is fully merged and no longer needed. Delete it.
hints: git branch lists old-idea next to main.
levels.successMessage: Deleting a branch only removes the label. Its commits are still in main's history.

levels.title: Branch from the past
levels.objective: Create a branch called hotfix that points at the commit before the latest one.
hints: git branch can take a second argument: where the branch should start.
levels.successMessage: A branch can start at any commit, not just the latest one.
